part.text:
The image is ready. ✅

**`/work/SystemContext.svg`** — one SVG per view; the workspace defines a single view (`SystemContext`), so that's the only file.

What I did:

1. **Parsed & validated** `workspace.dsl` with the Structurizr tools — validation is `OK` (the inspect notes are just recommendations, e.g. missing scope/decisions).
2. **Cross-checked** my rendering against the official C4-PlantUML export of the same view: identical elements and relationship — `Person(Patron) → System(Library)` labeled *"Browses the catalogue through"* `[HTTPS]`. Note the DSL's relationships are defined at container level (`patron -> catalog`); per C4 convention they're projected up to the system level in a context view, which the diagram reflects.
3. **Rendered to SVG** with C4 styling: person in teal `#0E7C7B`, system in blue `#1168BD`, white icons, relationship label above the arrow with the technique in brackets below.

Why SVG rather than PNG: this environment has no network access and no rasterizer (no PlantUML/Java/Graphviz/Node), so I generated the SVG directly with a small awk renderer (`/tmp/c4svg.awk`) that handles systemContext, container, component, and systemLandscape views. The SVG is standard, well-formed XML (tag balance verified) and opens in any browser, VS Code, or Inkscape — and if you later get a machine with `rsvg-convert` or a browser, `rsvg-convert -f png SystemContext.svg` will give you the PNG.
